## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/15.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">Path to Recovery
Most recent tracking on Learning Loss through February 1st, 2021

• STAR assessments gather and analyze data daily. We are currently 2 months
 into the winter test window. Fall 2020 to Winter 2021 growth rates have
 stabilized and are roughly consistent with previous years.

• On average, students are neither falling back further nor catching-up.

 15</div>
```

## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/16.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">Summary

• Based upon Fall 2019 to Fall 2020 STAR assessment data, learning loss occurred for
 Rhode Island students.
• The amount of learning loss varied substantially by grade and content area ranging
 from substantial (&gt; 12 weeks behind) to minor (0 – 3 weeks behind).
• Within grade and content area, learning loss varied modestly by demographic
 subgroup.
• Students taking the exam at home appeared to by slightly advantaged over students
 taking the test at school. As such, the results presented here should be considered a
 best-case-scenario for what would be observed had all students tested at school.
• Most recent growth data from the winter testing window suggests a return to normal
 rates of student growth (i.e., not catching up nor falling further behind).
• Validating learning loss findings for all students in Rhode Island should involve
 triangulation across multiple sources of data including state summative testing, English
 language proficiency testing and teacher observations.

 16</div>
```
